Answer: B
Reason: The CT images (Figures 1a-c) demonstrate diffuse, randomly distributed micronodules throughout the lung parenchyma, which is the classic radiographic appearance of miliary tuberculosis. This finding correlates strongly with the clinical history of prolonged fever and increased sedimentation rate, whereas the other options describe patterns (large nodules, peribronchovascular distribution, centrilobular nodules, or single mass) that do not match the imaging.
